title: Dango configuration
description: Dango's config.json, kept in ~/.config/dango and shared over git. Every setting is optional; anything omitted uses its built-in default. Unknown keys are preserved, so a newer Dango or a plugin can add to this file safely.

extensions.description: Per-extension settings, keyed by extension id such as dango.clipboard.

selection.description: How Dango reads the text you have selected.

excluded-applications.description: Applications where Dango must never send the copy chord to read a selection, comma separated and matched ignoring case. For editors that bind Ctrl+C to something of their own, such as a Helix keymap. Dango reads these directly where it can, and says it cannot read the selection otherwise.

hyperkey.description: A physical key remapped to act as the hyper modifier system-wide. Present means on; omit the block to turn it off.

key.description: The physical key to remap. Defaults to capslock.

shift.description: Whether Shift is part of the combination. Defaults to true; false emits Ctrl+Alt+Super, leaving typed characters unshifted.

tap.description: A key to send on a quick, solitary tap of the hyperkey, such as "escape". A hold, or a press combined with another key, still acts as the hyper modifier. Absent means a tap does nothing.

hotkey.description: A chord, either a portable string like "mod+shift+k" or a per-platform object. Modifiers: mod (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl on Windows), ctrl, alt, shift, meta, hyper. The key is a physical position such as space, k, or left.

enabled.description: Whether the extension runs. Absent means enabled.

preferences.description: The extension's preference values, overriding its declared defaults.

commands.description: Per-command settings, keyed by command id.

apps.description: Applications bound to global hotkeys, keyed by the name Dango shows for the application in root search. Read by dango.applications only.

providers.description: Model services, keyed by the name commands refer to them by. That name is also the key its API key is filed under in auth.json. Read by dango.ai only.

name.description: The application's shown name when it differs from the key, either one string or a per-platform object. An object with no value for the running platform means the entry is skipped there.

kind.description: The protocol the service speaks. "openai" covers any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, such as OpenRouter, LM Studio, or vLLM. "cli" runs a program on this machine that takes a prompt and prints an answer.

baseUrl.description: Where the service lives. Anthropic and Ollama have defaults; an OpenAI-compatible endpoint needs one.

model.description: The model used by a command that names this provider but no model of its own. A cli provider may leave it out and let the program choose.

command.description: The program to run, for a provider of the cli kind. Looked up on PATH.

args.description: What to pass the program. {prompt} and {model} are replaced where they appear; with no {prompt}, the prompt goes in on standard input.

alias.description: A short alias that matches this command in root search.

enabled.description: Whether the command is offered. Absent means yes; false removes a command the extension ships.

title.description: The title root search shows. Needed for a command the file defines from nothing. Read by dango.ai only.

prompt.description: What the model is asked, as a template. Placeholders: {{ selection }}, {{ clipboard }}, and any other name, which the launcher asks the user for. Read by dango.ai only.

provider.description: The provider this command uses, by its name under providers. Absent falls back to the extension default. Read by dango.ai only.

model.description: The model this command uses. Absent falls back to the provider's model. Read by dango.ai only.

thinking.description: How hard the model should think before answering. A model that cannot think ignores it. Read by dango.ai only.

output.description: What becomes of the answer: shown in the launcher, pasted into the application you came from, or copied. Defaults to view. Read by dango.ai only.
